papers.title: Magnetic pendulum under external excitation with state-dependent phase control
papers.abstract: The dynamics of a strongly nonlinear magnetic pendulum subjected to phase-controlled magnetic excitation is investigated experimentally and numerically. The main novelty of the study lies in introducing a state-dependent phase law, in which the phase of the coil current depends on the instantaneous angular position of the pendulum. In contrast to classical magnetic pendulum with external constant-phase excitation, this modification creates a feedback-type phase modulation and changes the timing of energy transfer between the electromagnetic actuator and the mechanical oscillator. A mathematical model of the system is derived using an experimentally identified magnetic torque and validated against laboratory measurements. The validation performed for the classical case confirms that the model reproduces the principal dynamical features observed experimentally. For the phase-controlled system, the results reveal a rich organization of regular and chaotic regimes, broad families of coexisting attractors, and a pronounced reorganization of the bifurcation structure relative to the constant-phase case. A particularly important result is the existence of a robust intrawell period-1 branch that persists over a wide range of excitation amplitudes despite substantial changes in the magnetic forcing strength. Energy analysis shows that this response is sustained by localized, phase-dependent bursts of magnetic power input that compensate dissipation on a cycle-by-cycle basis. Basin of attraction analysis demonstrates multistability and fractal basin boundaries, quantified using both box-counting dimension and boundary basin entropy. The obtained results provide new insight into phase-controlled energy transfer and attractor selection in nonlinear magneto-mechanical oscillators.

papers.title: From advancing to locked fronts: The rank-one limit of a family of strain-gradient plasticity models
papers.abstract: We study a one-parameter family of strain-gradient plasticity functionals on an annular domain under azimuthal shear, in which the defect energy penalizes the geometrically necessary dislocation density with exponent κ ≥ 1 : the rank-one model at κ = 1 and the quadratic model at κ = 2 . The central question is whether the qualitative behavior of the family depends on κ , and in particular whether the rank-one exponent is special. We find that, for every κ > 1 , the plastic response is qualitatively the same regardless of the domain size: plasticity nucleates at the classical threshold, the plastic zone advances monotonically from the inner boundary, and the entire domain eventually becomes plastic at a finite applied displacement. At κ = 1 , this picture changes. Depending on the domain geometry, one of two qualitatively distinct behaviors emerges, both absent for any κ > 1 : the entire domain may plasticize simultaneously, but only above an elevated nucleation threshold; or, above a critical domain size, the plastic front instead locks at a fixed position strictly inside the domain, unable to advance regardless of the applied displacement, with nucleation occurring at a different elevated threshold and the displacement required to fully plasticize the domain diverging as κ → 1 + . Neither behavior emerges gradually: the passage from κ > 1 to κ = 1 is an abrupt change, not a smooth transition. These results are established through exact analytical solutions, asymptotic analysis of the limit κ → 1 + , and finite element validation.
